opinions.rationale: Inverted prior: searched for a formal four-step discrepancy decomposition (ideal→target→identified functional→estimator) in TTE. Own prior_work (Moreno-Betancur arXiv:2405.10026) frames ideal/target/actual trials and urges explicit discrepancies but does not supply a quantitative decomposition of total discrepancy into scientific-target mismatch, mapping loss, and estimation error. Hernán–Robins 2016 and Hansford 2026 are design/guidance, not decomposition. Searches for estimand lineage, estimand distance, and four-transition decomposition in AJE/Epidemiology/IJE/Sim/BMJ/JAMA and arXiv 2024–2026 returned framing and reporting proposals (ICH E9(R1), TARGET) but no operational metric or software that separates those four transitions. Still open as stated.

Selective-inference and post-selection literature exists for covariates and models, not for human search over TTE protocol components (eligibility, grace period, washout, outcomes). TARGET and Hansford 2025–2026 report the final protocol; they do not correct coverage for data-dependent protocol selection. Outcome-blinded design splits and dated decision logs remain proposals, not standard practice or validated TTE-specific selective-inference procedures. No CRAN/GitHub change for TrialEmulation/lmtp/ltmle/gfoRmula treats the protocol as a random object. Open.

Registrations and TARGET record the final specification. Multiverse/specification-curve methods (e.g. Simonsohn et al.) and some observational-study preregistration guidance exist, but EU PAS / ClinicalTrials-style registries and TARGET do not require rejected alternatives, decision chronology, or outcome-blinded feasibility logs as first-class artifacts. Version-controlled hashed executable specs before outcome analysis are not standard. Cost of full multiverse remains unsolved. Open as stated.

Conceptual naming of substituted estimands is advanced by Moreno-Betancur ideal/target/actual trials and by operational TTE frameworks (Hernán–Robins components; Wang npj Digit Med 2026 operational EHR mapping). That is partial progress on making substitution visible. Missing pieces remain: a usable language for partially specified interventions, mandatory component-by-component conceptual vs operational tables with substituted estimand as headline, and criteria validated on benchmarking data for which substitutions preserve trial agreement. Not fully solved.

resolving_work.title: The ideal trial: defining causal estimands that balance relevance and feasibility in target trial emulations and actual randomized trials
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Partial: explicit ideal vs target vs actual trial discrepancies so unobservable components can be named as changed estimands rather than measurement error; does not deliver component mapping tables, partial-intervention language, or benchmarking criteria for innocuous vs question-changing substitutions.

resolving_work.title: An operational target trial emulation framework for causal inference using electronic health records
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Partial: works through operational realization of protocol components against EHR data, the setting where component substitution occurs; does not require substituted estimands as headline quantities or validation criteria for which substitutions preserve trial agreement.

opinions.rationale: Interference and cluster/population allocation have estimand frameworks (Papadogeorgou et al. 2019 Biometrics and related interference literature). Policy and NPI emulations appear increasingly, sometimes with cluster assignment made explicit. Still missing: standard protocol templates stating which seven components a policy/NPI can satisfy, estimands over observed version distributions when versions cannot be unified, and minimum jurisdiction-unit counts for credible assignment-level inference. Partial prior art on identification; gap on TTE protocol templates and unit-count guidance remains open.

resolving_work.title: Causal inference with interfering units for cluster and population level treatment allocation programs
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Partial: estimand framework for cluster and population-level allocation with interference; does not supply TTE protocol templates for policy/NPI, version-distribution estimands as default reporting, or minimum jurisdiction-level sample-size rules.
